svg.title: Photosynthesis practical
svg.desc: Choose the variables: Independent: lamp distance/light intensity. Dependent: oxygen production rate. Pondweed in sodium hydrogencarbonate solution; keep CO₂ supply, volume, plant and orientation constant. Control temperature: Use a water bath/heat shield and check with a thermometer. The lamp can heat the water. Keep background light steady. Use the same measurement period; avoid spills near electrics and hot-lamp burns. Collect the data: Measure source-to-plant distance; allow the plant to acclimatise. Collect oxygen volume over a set time using an inverted water-filled tube, or count bubbles. Repeat at several distances; repeat each condition and calculate a mean. Investigate anomalies. Calculate rate: Rate = gas volume/time. 3.6 cm³ in 4 min = 0.90 cm³/min. Bubble estimate: 48 in 2 min = 24 bubbles/min. Keep time/volume units consistent. More gas in a longer time is not necessarily a faster rate. Plot & explain: Plot rate on y-axis; intensity or 1/distance² on x-axis. Label units and use a suitable scale/best-fit curve. Closer lamp → greater intensity; rate rises while light limits it. Another limiting factor can cause a plateau. Limits & improvements: Unequal bubble sizes → count is approximate; measure gas volume instead. Some oxygen dissolves or is used in respiration; check collector for gas leaks. Repeats reduce random uncertainty; they do not fix heating, leaks or another uncontrolled variable.
